message.content:
Based on my search, here are examples of preventive medicine practices organized by the three main levels of prevention:

## Primary Prevention (Preventing Disease Before It Occurs)

Primary prevention focuses on avoiding the development of disease entirely through interventions before any signs of illness appear.

**Lifestyle and Behavioral Interventions:**
- Regular physical exercise and fitness programs
- Healthy eating habits and nutrition counseling
- Smoking cessation programs
- Limiting alcohol consumption
- Stress management techniques
- Digital detox and mindfulness/meditation practices (increasingly recognized in 2026)

**Medical Interventions:**
- **Immunizations and vaccinations** – considered the "gold standard" of prevention, including childhood vaccines, adult boosters, seasonal flu shots, and COVID-19 vaccines
- Dental cleanings and fluoride treatments
- Use of sunscreen to prevent skin cancer
- Contraception and safe sex practices

**Environmental and Safety Measures:**
- Handwashing and proper hygiene practices
- Fall prevention strategies for older adults
- Use of seatbelts
- Environmental protection (air and water quality control)
- Workplace safety protocols and ergonomic assessments

**Health Education:**
- Public health campaigns
- School-based health education programs
- Community wellness programs

## Secondary Prevention (Early Detection and Intervention)

Secondary prevention focuses on identifying diseases in their earliest stages when treatment is most effective.

**Screening Programs:**
- **Cancer screenings:** mammograms (breast cancer), colonoscopies (colorectal cancer), Pap smears (cervical cancer), prostate exams, skin examinations for melanoma, lung cancer screenings for high-risk individuals
- **Cardiovascular screenings:** regular blood pressure monitoring, cholesterol level checks
- **Metabolic screenings:** blood glucose tests for diabetes
- **Other screenings:** vision and hearing tests, depression screenings, osteoporosis screenings, HIV and STI testing

**Regular Medical Care:**
- Annual physical examinations and wellness checkups
- Well-child visits (including growth and developmental milestone assessments)
- Prenatal care (monitoring fetal development, screening for gestational diabetes)
- Routine medical exams to establish baseline health measurements

## Tertiary Prevention (Reducing Impact of Existing Disease)

Tertiary prevention aims to minimize complications and improve quality of life for those already diagnosed with conditions.

**Disease Management:**
- Rehabilitation programs (e.g., after stroke or orthopedic surgery)
- Chronic disease management (e.g., diabetes monitoring to prevent nerve damage, kidney problems)
- Disability management
- Use of preventive medications (e.g., anticoagulants to prevent blood clots, statins for cardiovascular risk)

## Public Health and Community-Based Preventive Strategies

**Population-Level Interventions:**
- Vaccination drives and immunization programs
- Tobacco control programs (counter-marketing, quitlines, smoke-free policies)
- Pandemic preparedness and response planning
- Community walking and fitness programs
- Free health screening events for underserved populations

**Policy and Environmental Changes:**
- Urban planning for active living
- Subsidies for healthy foods
- Clean water and air quality regulations
- Workplace wellness programs with health risk appraisals and incentives

These preventive practices have demonstrated significant returns on investment. For example, the North Dakota Diabetes Prevention and Control Program saved an estimated $9 million over three years (about a 30-to-1 return), and Alaska's comprehensive tobacco control program led to more than 27,000 fewer smokers and an expected $300 million in averted medical costs.

Sources:
1. https://mesafp.com/blog/what-is-the-best-example-of-preventive-care/
2. https://idcchealth.org/blogs/what-is-preventive-medicine-and-what-are-its-types/
3. https://www.scirp.org/journal/paperinformation?paperid=143897
4. https://campmedicine.org/blog/examples-of-preventive-medicine-treatments-from-a-primary-physician/
5. https://www.primaryhealthcare.scientexconference.com/sessions/Preventive-Medicine-and-Public-Health-Strategies
6. https://www.tfah.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Examplesbystate1009.pdf
7. https://www.auamed.org/blog/what-is-preventive-medicine/
8. https://www.floridamedicalclinic.com/blog/preventive-medicine-examples-why-its-important/
9. https://easyaidmedical.com/blog/preventive-healthcare-guide/.html
10. https://www.readkong.com/page/examples-of-successful-community-based-public-health-9307672
